label: fed-back q (original position 1-3) during copy, not on the final step
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input is q. Since copy-phase inputs are the model own previous outputs, this is q being fed back as original token 1, 2 or 3 (recall_idx 2-4). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. A q fed back from original position 0 (recall_idx 1) barely activates, q from position 4 or later does not activate at all, and the final copy step (to_go 0) is silent. Magnitude is largest when q was original token 1 (recall_idx 2; top examples like c q b ... <DEL> c [q]) and drops at later positions. Low-quartile activations are q at position 3 or a repeated q. Other tokens essentially never activate it.

issues: Minor: the false positives are concentrated at recall_idx 4, where the feature is unreliable. Precision there is 0.69 overall, 0.69 at to_go 1, 0.92 at to_go 2 and 0.91 at to_go >= 3, and recall_idx 4 holds only 7.5% of activation mass. Most of the 1575 test false positives come from this class. The explanation already says activation drops at later positions, so the label is not wrong, but recall_idx 4 is a weak, partial part of the feature rather than a clean one.

Minor overstatement: 'activation is largest at recall_idx 2' is barely true for 2 versus 3. Mean activation per firing step is almost the same (dev mass share per active step is 0.502/16337 vs 0.421/14087). The big drop comes at recall_idx 4.

The other claims hold. Copy phase holds 100% of activation mass, with 0 activations in the original or delimiter phases. q holds 100% of mass, and other tokens fire about 60 times out of 41k active steps. recall_idx 1 has precision 0.058 and 0.2% of mass. recall_idx 5 and above has about 40 activations. to_go 0 has precision 0.011. All the to_go 0 false positives that would otherwise appear at recall_idx 3 come from L=4 sequences on their final step, and to_go >= 1 removes them.
Test misses hold 0.3% of activation mass. They are weak activations on q at recall_idx 1 and on the first of two repeated q's, which matches the explanation.

Narrowing variants did not beat the predicate on test F1. Requiring rel_tok(1) != q gave 0.952, and requiring to_go >= 2 gave 0.878, both below 0.966. No systematic class of counterexamples is left beyond the noisy recall_idx 4 group.
